entries.name: Theresa Ann Walker

expected.charges: Freedom Ride participation — arrested Jackson, June 21, 1961.
expected.convicted: Unresolved — the arrest is documented; the disposition is not established in the CRDL record
expected.sentence: Arrested 1961-06-21. The Civil Rights Digital Library establishes the arrest and the identification photograph but not the disposition, any transfer to Parchman, or the release date — unresolved pending court, jail, or penitentiary records.

updates.sentence: Arrested June 21, 1961. Her handwritten jail timeline, described by the University of Richmond archivist, records five days in custody, June 21–26, 1961. The court disposition and any transfer to Parchman remain unresolved.

entries.rationale: University archivist describes her own jail timeline with both endpoints. Five days, no inferred Parchman transfer.

entries.name: Stephen L. Smith

expected.charges: Destruction or mutilation of a Selective Service registration certificate (draft card) under the 1965 federal law.
expected.sentence: Three years of probation; no jail or prison sentence.

entries.rationale: University history dates arrest; contemporary Daily Iowan dates conviction and probation sentence. No imprisonment inferred from probation.

entries.name: Suzette Bridges

expected.charges: Treaty fishing-rights activity at Frank’s Landing
expected.sentence: No individual jail booking or confinement established in the reviewed records.

entries.rationale: October 4, 1968 Militant page 9 names her among Olympia arrests during September fish-in activity. Exact day and jail duration remain unknown.

entries.name: Sid Mills

expected.charges: State fishing-law violations arising from treaty-rights fish-ins at Frank’s Landing
expected.sentence: Arrested during the Fish Wars; exact custody dates and durations not located.

updates.sentence: Arrested October 13, 1968 during the Fish Wars. Exact custody duration and release date remain unresolved.

entries.rationale: Howard Zinn and Roxanne Dunbar-Ortiz explicitly date the arrest. Separate 1970 Fort Lawton case preserved.

entries.name: Raymond Johnson

expected.charges: Kidnapping arising from the November 4, 1968 diversion of National Airlines Flight 186; aircraft-piracy count dismissed
expected.convicted: Yes; original sentence vacated and remanded
expected.sentence: Initially sentenced to 25 years; the Fifth Circuit vacated the sentence and remanded for resentencing. He also reported four years in a Cuban prison. Final U.S. release date not located.

entries.rationale: September 12, 1986 AP report says he returned Thursday night, September 11, matching existing U.S. arrest. No U.S. release inferred.

entries.name: Marc Edelman

expected.charges: Destruction of a Selective Service registration certificate (the November 6, 1965 Union Square, NYC draft-card burning).
expected.convicted: Three of the five (Cornell, Edelman, Lisker) were convicted — United States v. Edelman — and sentenced to six months.

updates.sentence: Six months imposed November 30, 1966; appeal announced. Actual admission, release, and time served remain unresolved.

entries.rationale: December 1966 Catholic Worker page 1 individually names Edelman with Cornell and Lisker and gives sentencing date. Imposed sentence not counted as actual custody.

entries.name: David Lering Richards

expected.charges: Breach of the peace — Freedom Ride arrival in Jackson, July 15, 1961.
expected.convicted: Unresolved — the arrest is documented; the disposition is not established in the CRDL record
expected.sentence: Arrested 1961-07-15. The Civil Rights Digital Library establishes the arrest and the identification photograph but not the disposition, any transfer to Parchman, or the release date — unresolved pending court, jail, or penitentiary records.

updates.sentence: Arrested July 15, 1961. The San Francisco Chronicle obituary reports three months served at Parchman for his Freedom Ride. Exact admission and release dates remain unresolved.

entries.rationale: Obituary identifies the carpenter, Joplin roadie and Freedom Rider and reports three months actually served. Retain month precision without fabricated endpoints.

entries.name: Archie Brown

expected.charges: Holding union office while a Communist under section 504 of the Landrum-Griffin Act
expected.convicted: Convicted in 1963; reversed after the Supreme Court invalidated the law in 1965
expected.sentence: Six months in prison; remained free during appeal and no service of the sentence was established.

updates.convicted: Convicted April 5, 1962; reversed after the Supreme Court invalidated the law in 1965

entries.rationale: May 18, 1962 Dispatcher page 1 explicitly dates conviction April 5 and sentencing May 4; bail continued during appeal. No actual imprisonment inferred.
